## Context

This is a scoped follow-up to #1 and the implementation in draft PR #2. The source snapshot is commit `9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8`; it is not a claim that the default branch already contains that work. Coordinate the implementation baseline with PR #2 or its merged successor. Issue creation and the ready-for-agent label do not authorize provider launches, trust/permission changes, audit adoption, billing changes or new spending. Follow the execution host’s current policy and preserve existing evidence.

## Triage evidence

- Confirmed static gaps in the current acquisition: required effective/remote-policy states remain explicitly unexposed, and helper-loader scope is conditional.
- These are Council integration/qualification gaps; this triage does not establish a new Cursor runtime denial.

**Redundancy check:** Inspected Cursor acquisition, its effective gate, preflight admission and existing provider-control tests. Existing related mechanisms do not satisfy the specific remaining contract below.

**Prior rejection check:** No rejection knowledge base or matching rejection record was present in the inspected checkout. No other follow-up issue existed at triage start.

## Dated source references

- [Cursor source/control acquisition](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/src/pilot/provider-controls.ts)
- [Per-route admission behavior](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/src/pilot/preflight.ts)
- [Provider input boundary](https://github.com/arduinitavares/the-council/blob/9aff16ceb97e9420ab346552c04405c38d2ffde8/src/pilot/provider-session.ts)

The agent-brief comment is the implementation contract. Parent #1 stays open until its independent operational acceptance criteria are met.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**State:** ready-for-agent, explicitly requested by the maintainer. This means the specification is ready; dependency or runtime gates are not implied to have passed.
**Summary:** Qualify Cursor packet boundaries, trust and helper-loader controls

**Current behavior:**
Cursor recipes acquire trust/configuration inputs and provide conditional helper guards, but still report effective packet-read/remote-policy/startup controls as unknown. Existing helper guards require the actual loader root to match the owned packet root. A configured sandbox flag or trust marker is not proof of the effective no-tool/no-helper boundary. No Cursor process or setting was touched during this triage.

**Desired behavior:**
Establish a supported, source-backed Cursor route for supplied-packet reading with exact workspace trust, effective read/Deny boundaries, correct helper-loader scope and startup-effect coverage before the one-way print input can execute. Preserve specific unknown/unsupported outcomes when the host cannot establish a required control.

**Key interfaces:**

- `inspectProviderControls()`, `existingCursorTrust()`, `ProviderRecipe` and `ControlFact` bootstrap/effective states.
- `workspace-trust`, `configured-read-boundary`, `packet-read-boundary-and-deny-rules`, `helper-loader-root`, `helper-guard-ownership`, `helper-and-startup-effect-enforcement` and `effective-input-gate`.
- The Cursor one-way print route and its pre-established effective-control/input gate.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Provide a current capability/source matrix covering trust scope, loader-root selection, ordered configuration, remote enterprise/team/plugin effects and effective read/tool/helper controls; separate configuration inputs from enforced observations.
- [ ] Add isolated offline regressions for absent/eligible/foreign trust, root mismatch, unreadable or unexposed policy layers, Deny preservation and missing effective controls. Unknown must not become verified.
- [ ] A helper guard is admitted only when the actual loader selects its owned root. Existing global/ancestor hooks and repositories remain untouched.
- [ ] No user/topic input reaches the Cursor process before all required controls are established. If the supported route cannot expose the required prevention boundary, retain a precise unsupported/unknown outcome rather than assuming post-input inspection prevents effects.
- [ ] Any live qualification uses a separately authorized exact host/model/action route, finite limits and positive lifecycle evidence. The issue itself does not revoke the current instruction to leave Cursor alone.
- [ ] Normal completion/cancellation and invalidation/reuse evidence must satisfy the existing native proof contracts before the route is declared qualified. Coordinate included-only billing with its separate follow-up.

**Out of scope:**

- Changing Cursor/global trust, permissions, settings, hooks, account state or Git roots under triage authority.
- Removing required controls, inferring them from launch flags, switching the xAI route, or using billing/quota as containment proof.
- Included-only billing integration and full Council execution.

**Execution and delivery:**
Work against a revision containing the relevant PR #2 implementation. Recheck the current tree and host policy. Supply portable offline coverage and a reviewable change or validation record, with fresh independent review of material work. Required live evidence must use already-authorized, qualified routes and finite declared call/deadline limits. If a required external capability or permission is unavailable, retain a precise blocker and leave operational completion open; do not substitute a diagnostics-only result for the requested behavior. No global settings, accounts, historical artifacts or unrelated work may be changed under this brief.


**Dependencies:** No sibling prerequisite. Runtime and authorization gates in the brief still apply.
